segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
Arghun, the king of kings, was struck with hemiplegia,
and he languished in sickness for about a month of days.
The wretched Jew, however, was anxious over his illness,
and with great diligence sought to treat him.
Now the emirs and grandees of the camp,
those who had been despised by that Jew,
when hope for Arghun's life was cut off,
as though that Jew had been the cause of Arghun's illness by his evil conduct,
began to roar like lions against the wretched man,
until he finished his life,
on Wednesday at the end of the Latter Kanun of that year [1291 of our Lord?].
Then God stirred up His wrath against the Jews everywhere.
As for this Sa'd al-Dawlah, the Sahib Diwan, they killed him there,
and they diligently sent couriers to all the lands under the rule of the Mongols,
and they seized his brothers and his relatives,
and bound them in chains,
and plundered their possessions,
and took their sons, their daughters, their male servants, their female servants, their livestock, and all their property.
And he who was killed among them was killed,
and those who were left returned to their former condition.
Whereas he who yesterday was a commander, binding and loosing,
and clothed in royal garments,
today was wrapped in sackcloth with blackened hands,
that is to say, he was a dyer and not a scribe,
and a peddler and not a commander.
The trial and wrath that were stirred up against the Jews at this time,
no tongue is able to utter,
nor any pen to record.
Now in Baghdad, when the murder of this Jew was heard of,
the Muslims armed themselves and went to the Jewish quarter,
because they all lived in one quarter there in Baghdad.
And when they sought to enter and plunder them,
the Jews stood against them stoutly,
and fought;
they killed and were killed,
and did not allow them to prevail over them.
For they say
that when this Jew became great and was exalted,
he commanded a palace to be built for him in Tabriz,
and hid a great number of jars full of gold and silver in its foundations.
And this became known only at that time,
when they were being tortured, and they revealed the places of the jars;
and thus they dug and brought them out.
